messages.content: my friend asked me to spend the whole day at her house. i would like to go, but i need to come home before dinner.
you can tell her you would like to visit for part of the day. being happy to see her does not mean you have to stay until dinner.
i think she wanted us to cook together in the evening. i do not want to say yes to that and then leave.
then explain the time before choosing the plan together. you could ask whether a morning or afternoon visit would still be good for her.
write a message that says i want to come and also says when i need to leave.
i would love to visit. i can spend some time with you in the morning or afternoon, but i need to be home before dinner. would that still work for you?
she answered that she is busy in the morning but free after lunch. what do i know now?
you know the morning will not work for her and that she is free after lunch. you still need to choose a time that gives you enough time to get home before dinner.
is it wrong to ask how long she wants me to stay?
no. asking can help you make a clear plan together. you can also say when you need to leave, rather than asking her to choose that for you.
give me just the next question to send.
would a visit after lunch work if i leave in time to get home before dinner?
write a story about a boy who thinks a plant needs water but wants to check before doing anything.

a boy saw a plant by the garden wall. its leaves looked different from yesterday. he thought it might need water and took a container to the kitchen. his grandmother asked what he had checked. he said he had only looked at the leaves. together, they went outside. she knew how to care for that kind of plant and helped him check it before doing anything. the boy put the container down and listened. later, he wrote a note about what he had learned. the note began with a question: what do i know, and what should i check?
what did the boy think before he talked to his grandmother?
he thought the plant might need water because its leaves looked different from yesterday.
tell the story again, but make it shorter. keep the part about asking before doing anything.

a boy saw a plant with leaves that looked different from yesterday. he thought it might need water. before doing anything, he talked to his grandmother. she knew about that kind of plant and helped him check it. he learned to ask what he knew and what he should check before choosing what to do.
was the first thought enough to know what the plant needed?
no. the boy had an idea from looking at the leaves. he needed more information before choosing what to do.
tell a short story about a woman who finds an old family photo. let it end with her calling her brother.

a woman was cleaning a shelf when she found an old photo inside a book. it showed her and her brother outside their first home. she remembered the blue door and the tree by the wall. her brother was holding a toy, and she was looking up at their father. she put the photo on the table and found her phone. she wanted to ask her brother what he remembered about that day, so she called him.
i like how it starts, but i want the end to be more quiet. she should write him a letter instead.
we can keep her finding the photo and change what she does next. after looking at it, she could sit at the table and begin a letter about the day in the picture.
write only the new end, starting after she puts the photo on the table.

she took a piece of paper and began a letter to her brother. she wrote about the blue door, the tree, and the toy in his hand. before finishing, she asked what he remembered about that day. she left the photo by the letter while she read what she had written.
give me only the last sentence.
she left the photo by the letter while she read what she had written.
what did i change about the story?
you changed how she sent her question to her brother. she wrote a letter instead of calling him. finding the old photo stayed part of the story.
my sister gave me a blue garment to use for a family visit. i liked it so much that i left it in my room when we came home.
it sounds as if you liked using it. did your sister say you could keep it, or did she give it to you just for the visit?
just for the visit. now i want to ask if i can use it again next week.
then ask before making that part of your plan. you can thank her for the first time and say you would like another turn next week.
should i return it first?
that would make clear that the first visit is over and you know the garment is hers. you can give it back and then ask about another day.
say that in a shorter way.
give it back after the first visit, then ask about using it another day.
write one message that thanks her and asks about next week.
thank you for giving me your blue garment to use. i really liked it. could i use it again next week, if you do not need it then?
if she says no, does that mean she was sad about giving it to me to use the first time?
no. her answer about next week does not tell us how she felt about the first visit. she may need it herself, or she may have another reason.

i have an old note and a new note about our trip. the old note says meet at the station in the morning. the new note says the trip is now in the afternoon, but the meeting place is the same. where and when should we meet?
at the station in the afternoon. the new note changes the time and keeps the place.
my brother read only the first note. what might he think?
he might think the meeting is still in the morning, because that is the only time he has read.
if he gives me the old time, should i think he knows it is wrong?

not from what you said. he could be using the old information without knowing about the new note. having the wrong information is different from knowing the correct information and saying something else.
what should i show him so we both know about the new plan?
show him the new note. he can read that the time has changed and that the place is still the same.
write a kind message to him.
there is a new note about the trip. we still meet at the station, but the time has changed to the afternoon. i can show you the note.
what detail should not change when i explain this?
the meeting place should stay the station. only the time changed.
write about a child who does something wrong while drawing and finds a way to keep going.

a girl was drawing a house for her grandfather. she wanted the roof to be red, but she chose a blue tool without looking. when she saw the blue line on the roof, she put the tool down and felt sad. her grandfather asked what she wanted the picture to show. she said it was a house where people would feel happy. he asked whether a blue roof could be part of that kind of house. she looked at the picture again. she added a blue door and made the window large. then she drew a family outside, with flowers along the wall. the picture was different from her first idea, but she was happy to keep it.
did her grandfather tell her that blue and red were the same color?
no. he helped her think about the goal of the picture. the roof was still blue, not red.
why did she feel sad at first?
she had wanted a red roof and saw that she had made a blue line instead.
what changed by the end?
she found a way to make the blue roof part of a picture she liked. she kept drawing instead of putting the picture away when she saw the wrong color.
can you make that answer less long?
she changed her plan and kept drawing until she liked the picture.
i asked my brother to help me write a letter. he wrote the whole thing himself, and now it does not sound like me.
you wanted help with your own letter, rather than someone else writing all of it. you could tell him which parts you want help with and which parts you want to choose yourself.
i need help making the order clear. i know what i want to say, but i keep moving the sentences around.
then you could ask him to help you choose the order while keeping your own words. for example: please help me put these ideas in a clear order, but let me write the sentences.
i also want him to tell me if the grammar is wrong.
you can ask for that too. help with grammar and the order can still leave the meaning and voice as yours.
what should i do with the letter he wrote?
you do not have to send it as your own letter. you could look at its order, choose anything useful, and then write the letter in your own words.
what if i want to keep one of his sentences?
you can choose to keep a sentence if it says what you mean. getting help does not mean you have to use every sentence he wrote.
give me one kind sentence to say to him.
thank you for helping me. i would like to keep my own words and get your help with the order and grammar.
if i ask did you not enjoy the film, and my friend says yes, do i know whether she enjoyed it?
that answer might not be clear. yes could mean she did enjoy the film, or she could be saying your words are right. asking her to say the full meaning would help.
what would be a clear answer if she enjoyed it?
i did enjoy the film.
and if she did not?
i did not enjoy the film.
why do those answers help more than just yes or no?
they say what happened without making you work out which part of the question the answer goes with.
i want to ask her again without making her feel she did something wrong.
you could say: i am not sure i understood. did you enjoy the film?
just give me the question now.
did you enjoy the film?
now make it about a book instead, but keep the grammar the same.
did you enjoy the book?
what if she has not finished reading it yet?
you could ask about the part she has already read instead of asking about the whole book.
say that as a simple question.
do you like the book you are reading?
we are playing a game. each person can take one piece on each turn. my cousin took one piece first and then two pieces on her next turn. did she keep to the rule?
not on the next turn. the rule says each person can take one piece on each turn. taking two pieces on one turn is different from that rule.
she said she kept to it on the first turn, so it should be fine.
keeping to it on the first turn does not mean the rule stops later. the words on each turn mean it is still the rule when another turn starts.
make that answer more simple.
she took one piece on her first turn, which was correct. on the next turn, she took two pieces, but the rule still said one piece for each turn.
i only told you about those pieces and the rule. do you know who will get the most pieces?
no. that is not enough information to know who will get the most pieces. you have not told me what will happen next or when the game will end.
please do not add a new rule about the end of the game.
okay. i will keep the rule you gave and leave out information you have not given.
say just what she should have taken on her next turn after the first one.
one piece.
make a story about two people who do not both know that a book has moved.

a father left his book on the kitchen table before going into the garden. while he was outside, his daughter needed room for drawing. she put the book on the shelf by the door and used the table for her paper. when her father came back, he looked at the table. he did not see the book and asked where it was. his daughter told him she had put it on the shelf. he found it there and sat down to read while she finished her picture.
where did the father look first, and why?
he looked at the table first because that was where he had left the book. he did not yet know his daughter had moved it.
where was the book when he looked at the table?
on the shelf by the door.
why are those two answers different?
one answer is about where he looked, using what he knew. the other is about where the book really was after his daughter moved it.
did his daughter move it because she did not want him to find it?
the story does not say that. it says she moved it to make room for drawing and told him where it was when he asked.
write a short answer he could give her after finding it.
thank you for telling me. next time, please let me know when you move my book.
i am making lunch for my cousin. i can make rice or soup. she said either is fine, but she has to leave soon after we eat.
then the time may help you choose. which meal can you have ready before she needs to leave?
the soup is already made. the rice has not been started.
that makes soup a useful choice today. you can have lunch together without using most of her visit to wait for the food.
she likes rice more, though. should i make it instead?
you could ask if she wants to wait, but she already said either meal is fine and that she needs to leave soon after eating. from those details, soup works well for the time you have.
is that the same as saying rice is always the wrong choice?
no. this is a choice for this visit. on another day, with more time, rice could work well.
write one sentence telling her what i am making and why.
i will make soup today because it is ready, so we can eat together before you need to leave.
now leave out the reason and just tell her the meal.
i will make soup today.
what did i ask you to leave out?
the explanation about the food being ready and the time before she leaves.
i want to finish a book i stopped reading last month, but i forgot some of the story. do i need to start at the first page again?
not always. you could look back at a few pages before the place where you stopped and see whether the important parts come back to you. if you still feel lost, reading more from the start could help.
i remember the people, but not why they were going to another town.
then the reason for the journey is a useful thing to look for. you do not need to remember every small detail before you read another page.
can you just tell me why they went?
i would need the name of the book or the part of the story about their plan. you have not given me enough information to know their reason.
i do not know the name right now. i think one person had a letter from her mother.
that might be important, but it does not tell us the reason for the journey. you could look for the letter in the pages you already read.
what should i write down when i find it?
write a short note about who sent the letter, what it said, and how it changed the plan. keep to the details the book gives.
i would like to read a little every day, but i keep making a large plan and then doing nothing.
a smaller plan might be more simple to begin. what is one time of day when you often have a quiet moment?
after breakfast, before i start work. i usually look at my phone then.
you could put the book where you have breakfast and read one page before looking at your phone. the first goal can be to begin, rather than to finish a large part of the book.
what if i only read a few lines?
that can still be part of learning to do something new each day. you can think about what made it possible to read and try again the next day.
i thought i had to read a whole page for it to be useful.
if you read less than a whole page, you still spent some time reading. you can try again the next day.
should i say the whole plan is wrong if i miss one morning?
one morning does not tell us whether the whole plan is good or wrong. you can start again at the next quiet moment.
keep the plan very short.
leave the book by your breakfast place and read a little before using your phone.
my neighbor wants to use my camera for a trip. i do not want to give it to someone else right now. can i say no and still be kind?
yes. you can give a clear answer and still be kind to your neighbor. you do not have to say yes just to make the message sound warm.
i do not want to make up a story about it being broken. it works fine.
then do not say it is broken. you can simply say you are keeping it for your own use right now.
write the message.
thank you for asking. i am keeping my camera for my own use right now, so i cannot let you take it on the trip. i hope your journey goes well.
would i be changing the meaning if i said maybe later instead of no?
maybe later leaves another day open as a possible choice. if you do not mean that, it could make your answer less clear.
i do not know what i will want later, but i know my answer for this trip.
then keep the answer about this trip. you do not need to choose an answer for every request that might come later.
give me a shorter answer about this trip only.
i cannot let you take my camera on this trip, but thank you for asking.
write a story about a person who thinks a clock may be wrong. do not use number words above ten.

a man looked at the clock in his kitchen and thought he had enough time before a visit. he made tea, sat down, and read a letter. after a while, he looked at the clock again. it still had the same time. he began to think it had stopped. he checked another clock before choosing what to do next. the kitchen clock was wrong, and he had less time than he first thought. he put the letter away, finished his tea, and got ready to leave. before going out, he left a note by the kitchen clock so nobody else would use it without knowing it was wrong.
give me just the part about what made him think the clock was wrong.
he looked at the clock again after a while, but it still had the same time.
what did he do before choosing what to do next?
he checked another clock.
why did he leave a note?
he did not want someone else to use the kitchen clock without knowing it was wrong.
was the letter the reason the clock stopped?
no. the story does not tell us why the clock stopped. reading the letter happened while he was at home, but that does not show it made the clock stop.
give a different last answer with no new facts.
no. the story gives no reason for the clock to stop. it only says how the man found out there was a problem.
i put a blue book on the shelf, a red book on the desk, and a green book by the window. i want you to answer only the question i ask, without adding the places of the other books.
okay. ask me about one book, and i will keep the answer to that question.
where is the red book?
on the desk.
what color is the book by the window?
green.
which book is on the shelf?
the blue book.
i move the green book to the table. where is the book that was by the window?
on the table.
why did you not answer by the window again?
because you changed its place. by the window makes clear which book you mean, but you have now said that book is on the table.
what happened to the blue book while i moved the green one?
you did not say the blue book moved. from the information you gave, it is still on the shelf.
now answer just the place of the green book again.
on the table.
did you need to know who lives in my house to answer those questions?
no. the color of each book and the places you gave were enough for those questions.
my cousin says some people in her school group like drawing. can i say everyone in her group likes drawing?
no. some does not mean everyone. she told you that people in the group like drawing, but she did not say that all of them do.
what if she knows three people who like it?
then she has information about those three people. unless those are all the people in the group, that still does not tell us everyone likes drawing.
she has not told me how many people are in the group.
then we do not know that number. you can still use the information she gave: some people in her group like drawing.
i also know one person in the group who does not like it.
then you know that everyone likes drawing is false. you know one person who does not like it.
use a more simple way to say your last answer.
then not everyone likes drawing. you know one person who does not.
does that mean nobody in the group likes drawing?
no. one person who does not like drawing does not mean nobody likes it. you already have information about people who do.
write one sentence that keeps both facts.
some people in the group like drawing, and one person you know does not.
you said my uncle was visiting today, but i told you he was coming tomorrow.
you are right. your uncle is coming tomorrow. i should use the day you gave.
please do not make a long explanation about why you got it wrong.
okay. i will keep the visit as tomorrow.
now help me plan what i can do today before he comes.
what would you like to have ready for the visit?
i want the kitchen table clear and a picture ready to show him. i also need to do my school work.
you could do the school work first if it needs to be finished today. then clear the kitchen table and choose the picture. you do not need to get ready as if the visit were happening this afternoon.
why is using the right day important for the plan?
because you have today to get ready before the visit tomorrow. a plan for someone coming today could make you feel you have very little time.
explain it without talking about feelings.
the visit is tomorrow, so today can be used to get ready. the visit is not taking place this afternoon.
now tell me just when my uncle is coming.
tomorrow.
tell a story about a girl who wants to help a friend and also visit her grandmother. both things should still be possible at the end.

a girl had said she would help her friend choose a book at the library. she also wanted to visit her grandmother that day. at first, she thought she had to choose between the two plans. then she asked her friend when he wanted to go. he said he was free in the morning. she called her grandmother, who said an afternoon visit would be good. the girl wrote both plans on a piece of paper. after breakfast, she met her friend at the library. they looked at books until he found one he wanted to read. after lunch, she went to see her grandmother. she told her about the book, and they spent a quiet afternoon together.
what did her grandmother say about visiting in the afternoon?
her grandmother said an afternoon visit would be good.
did the girl have to stop helping her friend to see her grandmother?
no. she found out when each plan could happen and did them at different parts of the day.
what did asking questions change?
it gave her the information she needed to put both plans in a useful order. before asking, she did not know when her friend and grandmother were free.
what was on the piece of paper?
both plans: the library in the morning and the visit to her grandmother in the afternoon.
i said the wrong word while reading to my school group. i keep thinking everyone will remember it all week.

that sounds hard. saying a wrong word can feel like a very large thing when it happens in front of other people. do you know that everyone is still thinking about it, or is that what you are worried about?
it is what i am worried about. one friend said she did not even hear the wrong word.

then you have one reply that is different from the thought that everyone heard the wrong word and will remember. your feelings are real, but they do not tell us what every person in the group is thinking.
i do not want to be told it was not important at all. it was important to me.
you are right that it was important to you. we can understand your feelings without saying that everyone else will think about the wrong word for a whole week.
can you say that with more simple words?
it was important to you, and i understand why you feel worried. that does not mean everyone else will keep thinking about it.
what is one small thing i can do before reading again?
you could read the first few lines to yourself once before you begin. keep the goal small: knowing how you want to start, rather than trying to make every word correct.
leave out the part about every word being correct.
read the first few lines to yourself once, so you know how you want to begin.
